about: Data of Learn lesson A9, How do heat waves, droughts, wildfires and cold snaps break energy systems? The hazards are stress tests on lesson A5's Plains Grid (a05-adequacy.json: the same illustrative fleet, the same 500 resampled weather years, seed 2025): each hazard's dates, sizes and the defenses' effects and yearly costs are illustrative, chosen to show the mechanisms the real events below record. A hazard is applied in every simulated year, so a result reads 'in a year when it strikes', not a forecast of how often it strikes. The events are real, each from a primary report, with dates. The reference block holds the stress tests' results at seed 2025.

hazards.label: Heat wave
hazards.what: Demand 7% higher; gas units lose 5% of their output in the heat.

hazards.label: Drought
hazards.what: Coal and combined-cycle units lose 15% of their output: cooling water too warm or too scarce.

hazards.label: Cold snap
hazards.what: Demand 12% higher; gas units lose 30% to frozen equipment and fuel, coal 10%, wind 30% to icing.

hazards.label: Wildfire shutoffs
hazards.what: A line is switched off in high wind: a third of the wind output and a quarter of the available combined-cycle output are cut off, and 5% of demand loses power directly.

defences.label: Winterize plants and wind turbines, secure dependable gas supply
defences.what: Cold-snap losses of gas, coal and wind output cut to a third (gas 30% to 10%).

defences.label: Cooling upgrades
defences.what: Drought losses cut to a third, heat-wave losses of units halved.

defences.label: Harden lines, narrower shutoffs
defences.what: Shutoffs cut 40% as much supply and as much demand.

defences.label: 500 MW 4-hour battery
defences.what: Charges from any surplus, covers shortfalls (lesson A5's battery).

defences.label: 500 MW demand response
defences.what: Agreed load cuts on call, at most 4 hours a day, with no rebound later (lesson A5's program).

costNote: Yearly costs in millions of 2025 dollars, illustrative: chosen to make the choice a trade-off, not estimates for any real grid.

prepare.label: FERC–NERC report on Uri
prepare.text: Finds that freezing and fuel problems caused 75.6% of the units' outages, derates and failures to start.

prepare.label: ERCOT's offer cap lowered
prepare.text: The high system-wide offer cap falls from $9,000 to $5,000 per MWh.

prepare.label: FERC–NERC report on Elliott
prepare.text: Freezing and fuel problems again cause most of the outages.

prepare.label: Cold-weather standard EOP-012-3 in force
prepare.text: Each generator owner must have and carry out plans to keep its units running in extreme cold.
